question: Under O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311, how many days does a Georgia property owner generally have to file an appeal from the mailing date of an assessment notice?
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311 gives a property owner 45 days from the mailing date of the assessment notice to file an appeal of taxability, uniformity of assessment, or value.

question: Under O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311, what is the standard forum to which a Georgia property owner may appeal an assessment on issues of taxability, uniformity of assessment, and value?
choice_b: The federal district court for the district where the property is located
choice_d: The Georgia Department of Community Affairs
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311 establishes the county board of equalization as the standard appeal forum for a property tax assessment on issues of taxability, uniformity of assessment, and value -- also available to appeal denial of a homestead exemption.

question: Under O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311, a taxpayer owns a nonhomestead commercial property with a fair market value exceeding $500,000. What alternative appeal forum, beyond the county board of equalization, may this taxpayer elect for matters of value and uniformity of assessment?
choice_a: The Georgia Supreme Court, as a direct first-instance appeal
choice_c: No alternative forum exists for any property regardless of value
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311 allows a taxpayer with a nonhomestead property (or wireless property) exceeding $500,000 in fair market value to elect to appeal matters of value and uniformity of assessment to a hearing officer, as an alternative to the county board of equalization.

question: Under O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311, besides the county board of equalization and a hearing officer (for qualifying high-value property), what third appeal option is available to a Georgia taxpayer?
choice_a: Nonbinding arbitration, in which an arbitrator determines fair market value based on evidence presented by both the taxpayer and the county
choice_b: A private mediation session with no evidentiary component of any kind
choice_c: A jury trial as the mandatory first step in every appeal
choice_d: There is no third option; only the board of equalization and hearing officer routes exist
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311 provides taxpayers the option of nonbinding arbitration, in which an arbitrator determines the property's fair market value based on evidence submitted by both the taxpayer and the county -- a third appeal pathway alongside the board of equalization and hearing officer options.

question: Under O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311, if a taxpayer is dissatisfied with the county board of equalization's decision, how many days does the taxpayer generally have to further appeal to superior court from the date the decision is delivered?
choice_d: There is no further appeal available beyond the board of equalization
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311 gives a taxpayer 30 days from the date the board of equalization's (or other appeal body's) decision is delivered to further appeal to superior court.

question: Under O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311, how far in advance of a board of equalization hearing may a taxpayer generally request the county assessor's witness list?
choice_b: The day of the hearing itself only
choice_d: No witness list disclosure right exists under Georgia law
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311 gives a taxpayer the right to request the witness list at least 10 days before the board of equalization hearing, part of the statute's procedural protections ensuring the taxpayer has adequate notice of the evidence the county will present.

question: A property owner receives an assessment notice and disagrees with the county's determination of the property's fair market value. As a matter of the general burden created by O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311's appeal framework, what should a real estate licensee advise the owner about acting promptly?
choice_a: There is no urgency at all, since Georgia property tax appeals may be filed at any time without limitation
choice_b: The owner must wait a full year before any appeal may be filed
choice_c: Appeals can only be filed once every five years regardless of the assessment notice date
choice_d: The owner should act within the statutory 45-day window from the mailing date of the notice, since delaying beyond that window risks losing the right to appeal that assessment cycle
explanation: Because O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311 sets a 45-day window from the assessment notice's mailing date to file an appeal, a licensee should advise a client who disagrees with an assessment to act promptly within that window rather than delaying, since missing it risks losing the appeal right for that assessment cycle.
